exercise.name: Lying Alternate Toe Touch Floor

reference.title: Lying Alternate Toe Touch Floor
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk flexion and rotation with hip flexion)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you lift and reach; inhale as you lower.

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, short squeeze, 1 s down
prescription.progression: Reach higher up the leg, then add a pause, then full V-ups

cues.text: Lie on your back, legs long, arms overhead on the mat.
Lift the straight right leg as you curl the shoulders up and reach the left hand toward the right foot.
Turn the shoulder toward the leg; touch the shin or the toes, wherever you reach with control.
Lower the leg and the trunk back to the mat with control.
Repeat with the left leg and the right hand.

mistakes.mistake: Yanking with the arm and neck
mistakes.fix: Lead with the chest and the shoulder; the arm just follows.

mistakes.mistake: Bending the lifted knee to reach the foot
mistakes.fix: Keep the leg straight and touch the shin if the foot is out of reach.
Press the resting heel into the mat.

kinematics.norm: Shoulder blades off the mat with a turn toward the lifted leg (clinical opinion)
Opposite shoulder turns toward the leg (Crommert 2021: twisting curl-up)
Straight leg raised toward vertical (clinical opinion)
Hand reaches the shin or the foot (clinical opinion)
About 1 s up and 1 s down (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #11780, Lying Alternate Toe Touch Floor, video (movement reference; page not readable here)
Crommert, Bjerkefors, Tarassova and Ekblom 2021, abdominal muscle activation during common modifications of the trunk curl-up exercise (J Strength Cond Res 35(2):428-435; PMID 29319600)
Escamilla et al. 2006, electromyographic analysis of traditional and nontraditional abdominal exercises: implications for rehabilitation and training (Phys Ther 86(5):656-671; PubMed 16649890)
Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Repeated loaded spinal flexion is a concern for some backs (Axler and McGill 1997 on spine loads in sit-ups and curl-ups); keep the curl moderate.
modify: Knee of the resting leg bent, foot flat.
Reach to the knee instead of the foot.
Pregnancy, postpartum or diastasis recti: get cleared first, and avoid long supine work later in pregnancy.
regressions: Bend the lifted knee a little.
Crunch with a reach to the knee.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the head and shoulder blades off the mat for each reach; curl-ups with a twist keep rectus abdominis busy while adding oblique work (Crommert 2021; Escamilla 2006).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: The right external oblique with the left internal oblique turn the left shoulder toward the right foot; the other side takes over on the next rep (Crommert 2021: twisting curl-ups raise oblique activity).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: The left external oblique with the right internal oblique turn the right shoulder toward the left foot (Crommert 2021).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Lift the straight right leg toward vertical (clinical opinion; Andersson 1997 on hip flexor work in leg raises).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Lift the straight left leg toward vertical (clinical opinion; Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight and the legs long (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Reaches the arm up toward the foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Reaches the arm up toward the foot (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: The back of the lifted leg lengthens as the straight leg rises (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: The back of the lifted leg lengthens as the straight leg rises (clinical opinion).

phases.label: Right leg up, left hand reaches
Left leg up, right hand reaches

guides.label: Left hand reaches to the right foot
